Article Title: In 2015, a North Bondi beach house sold for A$4 million; 11 years later, it fetched A$17.4 million; records now reveal Nando’s billionaire owner Richard Enthoven as the mystery buyer
Article Text:

A beach house on the Ben Buckler headland has sold for A$17.4 million. This is more than four times what the same property fetched in 2015. The mystery buyers of this laid-back coastal luxury home are a couple better known for their chicken than their real estate! Nando’s billionaire owner Richard ‘Dick’ Enthoven and his wife, Karen, are the buyers, according to a report by the Wentworth Courier.The house sits at 148 Hastings Parade, in the stretch of North Bondi that is fast becoming a ‘billionaire’s row’, with Afterpay founder Nick Molnar, Australia’s youngest billionaire, living just up the road and Lorna Triguboff, the daughter of billionaire property developer Harry Triguboff, who is worth $32 billion, living further along.The sale of this four-bedroom beach house was completed on 20 June through a private treaty via Raine & Horne Double Bay. Ric Serrao handled the deal. Neither the agency nor the buyers have said much about the sale. The price itself is on the public record, which is how the details came to light.Richard ‘Dick’ Enthoven and his wife, Karen, are the mystery buyers, according to the outlet. Richard is a South African billionaire who owns the Nando’s restaurant chain and the insurer Hollard. The settlement records show that the property is now registered in Karen Enthoven’s name.The previous owner was Adrian Reef, director of the corporate debt firm Reefine Capital.This is not your regular beach shack. The beach house was designed by a leading Sydney architect and built by Pamment Projects, an award-winning builder. ‘This extraordinary freestanding residence sets a new benchmark for refined beachside living, where laid-back luxury and design excellence exist in perfect harmony,’ the listing says. The house has four bedrooms and three bathrooms.The house has changed hands only twice in 80 years, and the buyer gets a home built around how people actually live on the coast. The curated palette of European oak, timber and natural stone brings a beach-inspired aesthetic. The house is designed for year-round indoor and outdoor living and entertaining. It is divided into two separate indoor and outdoor zones, allowing a family to spread out without losing the feeling of being together. Soft, sandy tones keep the look relaxed, while the finishes remain polished. The north-facing backyard features a heated mosaic pool with jets, and both the front and rear alfresco areas catch the ocean breeze. The rear barbecue runs directly off the gas mains, making weekend cooking easy. The expansive ocean-view terrace, with its resort-style back garden, also makes the property perfect for buyers seeking a laid-back, luxurious home.Inside, every bedroom has a built-in wardrobe, air conditioning and ceiling fans. The main suite looks out over the water and features a freestanding bath and a rain shower. Skylights fill the custom study and the rest of the home with daylight. Zellige tiles and heated floors feature in the laundry and bathrooms. The house is designed with comfort and safety in mind. Daikin zoned air conditioning, an Escea gas fireplace, ceiling-mounted Sonos speakers and an alarm system are among its features. The Caesarstone kitchen has gas appliances, two Bosch dishwashers, an island breakfast bar with a wine fridge tucked underneath, and a full butler’s pantry.A rear gate opens onto the North Bondi golf course and its walking tracks, while the garage has room for three cars, plus storage or a man cave. From there, the village cafés, cliff walks and Bondi Beach are all within easy reach.Meanwhile, the Enthovens already own Greenoaks Cottage, a nine-bedroom 1850s mansion in Darling Point. They bought it in late 2019 for $18 million from Anne-Maree Kerry, a former Olympic gymnast, and Phil Kerry, the boss of recruitment firm K2.The couple also owned a waterfront home in Point Piper, which sold for $21.8 million to developer Barrie Nesbitt and his wife, Emma. It is not yet clear whether the North Bondi house is intended as a family home or a holiday escape.
Article Summary: The house sits at 148 Hastings Parade, in the stretch of North Bondi that is fast becoming a ‘billionaire’s row’ The sale of this four-bedroom beach house was completed on 20 June through a private treaty via Raine & Horne Double Bay. Richard ‘Dick’ Enthoven and his wife, Karen, are the mystery buyers.

Article Title: An Arizona homebuilder spent years and hundreds of thousands of dollars turning his backyard into one of America’s largest private garden railways, with nearly 4,000 feet of track and hundreds of trai
Article Text:
Sirrine had been interested in model railways from a long time (Photo: All About Mesa AZ. Image enhanced by AI)

How an empty backyard became a railway

Electrical problems led to a different operating system

The features Sirrine's most proud of

An Arizona businessman who made his name in homebuilding and design spent years and hundreds of thousands of dollars turning his backyard into one of the largest private garden railways in the United States. Dennis Sirrine, began building the Palo Verde & Southwestern Railroad in January 2004. The project eventually featured nearly 4,000 feet of railway track and a collection of hundreds of model train cars.According to the PBS programme Tracks Ahead, Sirrine used his experience in construction to develop the large outdoor railway. The layout included winding tracks, artificial mountains, lakes and rivers, with sections raised several feet above the ground to make the trains easier to see.Sirrine had been interested in model railways from a long time. During his years as a general contractor, he sometimes incorporated railway layouts into the houses he designed. These involved installing wooden shelves near ceiling height, laying tracks on them and allowing model trains to travel through several rooms.His backyard railway, however, was a much larger undertaking. What began as an empty piece of land required extensive construction, repeated modifications and a complicated operating system.Sirrine told PBS that some parts of the railway had to be built more than once before he was satisfied with the results.When construction began in January 2004, Sirrine's backyard was largely flat, with no existing railway infrastructure. After studying garden railways elsewhere in the country, he decided that an elevated layout would provide a better viewing experience than tracks placed directly on the ground.The railway was therefore constructed at heights ranging from 30 inches to six feet. According to Sirrine, approximately 1,000 cubic yards of soil were brought onto the property to raise different sections of the layout.The raised tracks allowed visitors to watch the trains without having to bend down or kneel. Sirrine also designed the surrounding landscape to resemble real railway routes, incorporating changes in elevation, curves, lakes and rivers.His previous construction experience helped him undertake the project, but it did not prevent problems. Sirrine said he had worked in the construction industry for 17 years and understood the building process. Even so, several sections did not turn out as planned.He estimated that nearly half the layout had to be removed and rebuilt because of construction problems or incorrect advice about particular methods. Repeating completed work became one of the project's biggest challenges.Building the tracks was only part of the work. Sirrine also had to develop a system that could operate different types of model locomotives across the extensive railway.The original electrical arrangements involved approximately 1,000 feet of wire and 10,000 feet of conduit. Looking back, Sirrine said he would have preferred battery-powered trains from the beginning.The railway eventually used a combination of battery power and electricity supplied through the tracks. This arrangement also allowed visitors who owned electrically powered locomotives to operate their trains on his layout.Another major challenge involved the turnouts, or switches, which allow trains to move between different tracks. Sirrine had observed electrical switches developing corrosion and operational problems on other garden railways.Concerned about their reliability in Arizona's climate, he chose air-powered switches manufactured by the California and Oregon Coast Railway company in Oregon. The system operated using a compressor rather than relying on electrical switches.Sirrine told PBS that the air-powered system had worked reliably after installation, resolving one of the most difficult operating problems he had faced.Despite the project's size, Sirrine identified two particular achievements when discussing his railway with PBS- the accuracy of the tracks and the construction of the artificial mountains.The tracks were laser-levelled to keep them straight and ensure smooth changes in elevation. According to Sirrine, visitors had placed video cameras on flatbed railway cars and recorded their journeys around the layout. They were impressed by how smoothly the trains travelled.Meanwhile, the mountains required a different construction method. Sirrine used flat concrete panels designed to resemble rock, breaking them into sections before arranging, grouting and staining them to create realistic desert formations.The resulting landscape formed part of a railway designed to combine model trains with the appearance of natural terrain.
Article Summary: Dennis Sirrine began building the Palo Verde & Southwestern Railroad in January 2004. The project eventually featured nearly 4,000 feet of railway track and a collection of hundreds of model train cars. The layout included winding tracks, artificial mountains, lakes and rivers.

Article Title: Demi Moore owns 2,000 dolls, including one-of-a-kind art pieces, and once planned to turn her extraordinary collection into a museum
Article Text:
Image: AP

How Demi Moore's 2,000-doll collection began

Why Moore considers her dolls works of art

The museum she once wanted to establish

Moore has stopped actively collecting dolls

The lasting appeal of Moore's extraordinary collection

Hollywood actor Demi Moore has an unusual passion that extends beyond the screen, with a collection of around 2,000 dolls, many of which she considers contemporary works of art. Unlike conventional playthings, these pieces are hand-sculpted figures designed to capture human expressions and emotions in miniature. Moore discussed her collection in a September 2024 interview with The Guardian, revealing that she still owned the dolls but had not added to the collection for a long time. The actor had also considered turning her extraordinary assortment into a museum, an idea she discussed publicly years earlier. Her fascination began with a doll gifted by her then-husband, Bruce Willis, after the birth of their daughter, eventually growing into a collection featuring unique creations by French artist Anne Mitrani.Moore traced the origins of her collection to a gift from Bruce Willis, whom she married in 1987. In a January 2025 interview with W Magazine, she recalled that she had recently given birth when Willis brought home a doll created by French artist Anne Mitrani after travelling for a film promotion trip.Their daughter was approximately a week old at the time. Moore described the doll as an introduction to a new kind of play and an experience that allowed her to explore emotion through an unexpected medium.The gift sparked an interest that gradually developed into a collection of approximately 2,000 dolls.Rather than collecting conventional toys, Moore became drawn to figures that resembled real people and conveyed distinct expressions. Over time, the collection grew to include numerous individually crafted pieces, particularly works associated with Mitrani, whose creations helped shape Moore's appreciation for art dolls.For Moore, the dolls are more than decorative objects or childhood playthings. She has described them as contemporary art pieces, many of which are one-of-a-kind creations shaped by the artist's attention to human expression and detail.In her W Magazine interview, Moore discussed how the figures capture moments of emotion through their faces, poses and carefully sculpted features. Their lifelike appearance distinguishes them from mass-produced dolls, giving each piece an individual character.Mitrani's work occupies a significant place in the collection. The French artist is known for creating detailed figures that resemble miniature human beings, with an emphasis on expressions and realistic features. Moore's interest in these works reflects her appreciation for the craftsmanship involved in translating human characteristics into small sculptural forms.Moore's ambition to create a museum for her dolls dates back several decades. A The Washington Post feature published on July 31, 1999, documented the collection and reported that a curator associated with the doll world had been helping organise it while travelling internationally to find additional pieces.The idea resurfaced in a 2007 feature published by Tribute magazine. Moore discussed her collection of antique dolls, many created by Mitrani, and said she was considering opening a doll museum. She also described the figures as remarkably lifelike works of art.The 2007 feature reported that individual pieces could cost as much as $20,000, highlighting the specialist market for unique art dolls. Moore also expressed the belief that her collection might be the world's largest collection of Mitrani's work.In her September 2024 interview with The Guardian, Moore returned to the museum idea, explaining that she had wanted to establish a dedicated space because some of the dolls were extraordinary works of art. The concept reflected her view that the pieces deserved to be appreciated as artistic creations rather than treated simply as personal possessions.Although Moore confirmed in 2024 that she still owned the collection, she said she had not added to it for a long time. In her January 2025 interview with W Magazine, she also discussed having moved away from actively collecting the dolls.The collection nevertheless remains an unusual part of her personal interests. Her comments reveal a long-standing fascination with objects that inspire curiosity through their scale, craftsmanship or unexpected appearance.During her Guardian interview, Moore also spoke about collecting objects of unusual sizes, including oversized and miniature items. Among the larger pieces she mentioned were a six-foot butcher's knife, a pair of three-foot scissors, boxing gloves and a clipboard. She explained that she finds unusual scale interesting and enjoys the playful effect of seeing familiar objects transformed into something unexpected.This interest in objects that challenge ordinary expectations provides another perspective on her doll collection. Both miniatures and oversized items alter how people perceive familiar forms, drawing attention to their details and proportions.Moore's collection stands out because of its scale and the artistic character of its individual pieces. What began with a gift from Willis developed into an assortment of approximately 2,000 dolls, many associated with Mitrani's distinctive approach to sculpting lifelike figures.Her long-standing interest in creating a museum also reflects a desire to present the dolls as works of art worthy of public appreciation. Through their carefully crafted expressions and individual features, the figures occupy a space between sculpture and collectible art.
Article Summary: Demi Moore has a collection of around 2,000 dolls, many of which she considers contemporary works of art. Her fascination began with a doll gifted by her then- husband, Bruce Willis, after the birth of their daughter. The actor had also considered turning her extraordinary assortment into a museum, an idea she discussed publicly years earlier.

Article Title: Barack Obama’s Chicago presidential centre grew from a $500 million proposal to nearly $850 million project by 2026; more than a decade after plans emerged, it opened amid debate over Jackson Park
Article Text:
Obama Presidential Center cost is backed by private donations

Barack Obama’s presidential centre takes shape on a 19-acre Chicago site

Obama Presidential Center projects up to 1 million visitors a year

Construction faced years of opposition and review

Barack Obama’s presidential centre opens in Chicago after years of delays and debate

Barack Obama’s presidential centre in Chicago was planned as a major investment in the city’s South Side, the neighbourhood that shaped much of his personal and political life. The planning process began in 2014, and Chicago’s South Side was selected for the project in 2015. Jackson Park was chosen as the specific site in July 2016, followed by design reviews, a federal review and legal challenges before construction began in 2021.According to PBS News, the centre was backed by private donations which reveal the project's estimated cost that rose from $500 million to roughly $830 million by 2021 further refined to approximately $850 million by 2026.Set within Jackson Park beside Lake Michigan, the development was designed to bring together a museum, educational facilities and public spaces. Yet its ambitions have also drawn scrutiny over the use of historic parkland, tree removal and fears that rising property prices could put pressure on long-standing residents.The Obama Presidential Center is being financed through private contributions rather than public funding for its construction. When the Obama Foundation released figures in August 2021, the projected cost had risen to approximately $830 million from an initial estimate of $500 million.By 2026, the reported cost had increased further to around $850 million, according to PBS News. The rising estimates reflect the scale of a project that spent years moving through planning, legal challenges and regulatory review before construction began in September 2021.The financial commitment is tied to the Obama Foundation’s plans for a permanent institution in Chicago. Unlike a conventional museum devoted primarily to displaying historical objects, the centre is intended to bring together exhibits, educational activities and public amenities. The former president has described the project as a way to recognise the community that shaped his life while creating a place with uses extending beyond his time in office.Private fundraising also places the foundation at the centre of the project's long-term development. The 2021 figures offered a snapshot of the expected construction bill, rather than a final account of what the completed institution would cost to build and operate.The centre occupies a 19-acre site within Jackson Park, a historic public landscape on the shore of Lake Michigan. The wider park covers hundreds of acres and has long been part of Chicago's civic and recreational life. Choosing this location connected the presidential centre to the South Side, but it also made the development more contentious than a project on an ordinary vacant site might have been.Obama's relationship with the area predates his presidency. He worked as a community organiser on Chicago's South Side before entering electoral politics, later taught law at the University of Chicago and built his family life in the city. Michelle Obama also grew up on the South Side. The foundation's decision to establish the centre there reflected those connections, placing the institution near places that played a part in the couple's lives.At the groundbreaking ceremony on 28 September 2021, Michelle Obama said, “This city, this neighborhood courses through my veins and defines me at my very core.""This substantial investment in the South Side will help make the neighborhood where we call home a destination for the entire world."The plans outlined in 2021 included a museum, a branch of the public library, an athletic centre, a test kitchen and a children's play area. The campus was designed to combine presidential history with facilities intended for public use, rather than operate solely as a repository for documents and memorabilia.As reported by PBS News in 2021, the Obama Foundation projected that the centre could attract around 750,000 visitors annually. By 2026, estimates had been refined, with approximately 600,000 visitors expected each year at the ticketed museum and up to 1 million anticipated across the campus’s free public amenities.The development was also expected to bring new trees and employment opportunities to the site. Obama presented those additions as part of the centre's potential contribution to the surrounding area, alongside its cultural and educational role.The groundbreaking followed a lengthy period of disputes over the project's location and potential consequences. Legal challenges and a federal review delayed progress, in part because Jackson Park is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The site's protected status meant that the development required scrutiny beyond the ordinary planning process.Environmental concerns became a separate point of contention. Critics objected to the use of parkland and the removal of trees, arguing that the project would reduce green space in an established public park. During the September 2021 ceremony, an aircraft flew over the site carrying a banner urging the organisers to stop cutting down trees and move the centre elsewhere.Barack Obama’s presidential centre finally opened to the public on Chicago’s South Side on 19 June 2026. The opening marked the completion of a long-running project intended to preserve Obama’s presidential legacy while creating a space for education, public engagement and community activities. Although the centre was designed to attract visitors and investment to the neighbourhood, questions about historic parkland, environmental changes and housing affordability remain part of the wider discussion about its impact. Its lasting success will depend on whether the opportunities it creates benefit the surrounding community as well as visitors from around the world.
Article Summary: The Obama Presidential Center is being financed through private contributions rather than public funding for its construction. When the Obama Foundation released figures in August 2021, the projected cost had risen to approximately $830 million from an initial estimate of $500 million. By 2026, estimates had been refined, with approximately 600,000 visitors each year at the ticketed museum and up to 1 million anticipated across the campus’s free public amenities.

Article Title: Shakira contributed $3.68 million toward an $8 million school in Cartagena that opened in 2014; 12 years later, the campus still serves more than 1,000 children from the city every year
Article Text:
Shakira

A school in a vulnerable neighbourhood

Image courtesy: Shakira/ Instagram

What the campus provides

Shakira’s role through Pies Descalzos

A lasting educational legacy

Image courtesy: Shakira/Instagram

Why access to education is important

From a celebrity donation to community infrastructure

Shakira wanted a Bollywood touch for ‘Hips Don’t Lie’

In 2014, Colombian singer Shakira helped open a major new school in one of Cartagena’s most vulnerable neighbourhoods. Through her Fundación Pies Descalzos, she contributed $3.68 million toward the $8 million construction of the Institución Educativa Fundación Pies Descalzos Lomas del Peyé, a 7,780-square-metre campus in the La María neighbourhood. The school was designed for up to 1,700 students and continues to serve more than 1,000 children each year, according to Fundación Pies Descalzos and reports published by La Nación.Twelve years after its opening, the campus remains a visible example of how celebrity philanthropy can support long-term community infrastructure. It was not a short-term donation or a one-off event, but a school built to provide classrooms, meals, recreation, and educational opportunity for children living in an area with significant social and economic challenges.Lomas del Peyé is located in La María, a neighbourhood in Cartagena that Fundación Pies Descalzos identifies as one of the city’s most vulnerable areas. The school serves children living in informal settlements, particularly in areas behind the city’s airport. The campus was built on a 7,780-square-metre site and was designed to accommodate students across early childhood, primary, and secondary education. Reports say the project had capacity for around 1,700 students of different ages.The school opened in February 2014 after an $8 million construction project, as pee reports. Shakira’s contribution accounted for about 46 percent of the total budget, while the remainder came from public and private partners.The Lomas del Peyé school was designed as more than a collection of classrooms. Fundación Pies Descalzos says the campus includes a library, laboratory, bilingual classrooms, technology room, school dining hall, sports courts, recreational areas, and 44 sanitation facilities. Those facilities matter because a child’s ability to learn depends on more than lessons. Safe classrooms, clean bathrooms, nutritious meals, and spaces for play and exercise all help create the conditions for regular attendance and stronger educational outcomes.The foundation describes its schools as “open-door” spaces intended to serve the wider community. The goal is to make the campus a centre for development and opportunity, rather than a facility used only during school hours.Shakira founded Fundación Pies Descalzos to support education and early childhood development in Colombia. The foundation’s work focuses on children and young people in vulnerable communities, with an emphasis on improving access to quality education.Her $3.68 million contribution to Lomas del Peyé represented nearly half of the school’s total construction cost. Reports say the donation was made through the foundation and formed part of its broader effort to expand educational access in Cartagena.The project also created hundreds of jobs during construction, according to reports on the initiative. That added a short-term economic benefit to the neighbourhood while the school itself was designed to deliver a long-term social return.Twelve years after opening, the school continues to serve more than 1,000 girls and boys annually. Fundación Pies Descalzos says the campus remains active in La María, providing education to children from one of Cartagena’s most vulnerable communities. The school was the first Pies Descalzos institution built in Cartagena. Its continued operation shows how investment in school infrastructure can have a lasting impact, especially when it is paired with programmes that support attendance, learning, and community participation.The campus also forms part of a wider network of Pies Descalzos education projects throughout Colombia. The foundation has built or supported schools and educational facilities in Barranquilla, Cartagena, Quibdó, and La Guajira, with a focus on children facing poverty, displacement, or limited access to services.School can offer stability for children in communities impacted by poverty and informal housing, which they may not be able to find anywhere else. A reliable campus with meals, sanitation, technology, and recreational space can reduce barriers that prevent children from staying in education.This understanding is reflected in the Lomas del Peyé project.The Foundation wanted to improve access to education and the quality of the environment in which children learn by building a large, well-equipped school in La María.The school’s capacity for 1,700 students also signals an ambition beyond immediate enrolment. Even though it currently serves more than 1,000 children each year, the campus was designed to accommodate growth and serve a broader population over time, as per reports.Shakira’s contribution is often reported as a celebrity donation, but its most important legacy is the school itself. The campus has provided education to thousands of children since 2014 and continues to operate in a neighbourhood where access to quality schooling can be limited.The project shows how philanthropy can work best when it creates durable public assets. Rather than offering temporary aid, the investment helped build a permanent educational institution with classrooms, meals, sports facilities, and community spaces.Twelve years later, Lomas del Peyé remains a working example of that approach. Shakira’s $3.68 million contribution helped create a school that continues to welcome more than 1,000 children from Cartagena every year.
Article Summary: Shakira founded Fundación Pies Descalzos to support education and early childhood development in Colombia. The foundation’s work focuses on children and young people in vulnerable communities, with an emphasis on improving access to quality education. Lomas del Peyé school was designed as more than a collection of classrooms. It includes a library, laboratory, bilingual classrooms, technology room, school dining hall, sports courts, recreational areas, and sanitation facilities.

Article Title: Houthis target Saudi Aramco compound, limited fire reported
Article Text:
A missile attack targeted Saudi Aramco's administrative building, damaging upper floors of the headquarters complex (Reuters)

Saudi Aramco’s administrative building in Dhahran was hit in a missile attack that triggered a limited fire, Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry said on Wednesday, as the kingdom faced a fresh wave of Houthi missile and drone attacks.No casualties were reported in the incident, while Saudi authorities said they had intercepted missiles and drones targeting several parts of the country.A company source told Reuters that a ballistic missile struck the Aramco headquarters complex, damaging the top three floors of an office tower. The complex houses a major operations centre overseeing the state-owned oil giant’s network of onshore and offshore oil rigs, pipelines, refineries and export terminals.The energy ministry said authorities responded to the incident late on Tuesday and took the necessary measures.The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a missile over Dhahran, with fragments falling in a residential area. Authorities also reported intercepting and destroying missiles and drones targeting the capital, Riyadh, and Saudi Arabia’s southern region.In Riyadh, four people, including two women, a man and a child, were injured after fragments from two intercepted Houthi missiles fell in the capital, Saudi civil defense said on Wednesday. The debris also caused limited damage to 15 homes, a civil defense spokesperson said.The latest attacks follow a series of Houthi strikes on Saudi targets over the past week. Riyadh’s international airport has faced four strikes, including a ballistic missile attack on Saturday that killed 13 people.
Article Summary: Saudi Aramco's administrative building in Dhahran was hit in a missile attack that triggered a limited fire. No casualties were reported in the incident, while Saudi authorities said they had intercepted missiles and drones targeting several parts of the country. The latest attacks follow a series of Houthi strikes on Saudi targets over the past week.

Article Title: UK PM says Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote, warns Europe faces same threat
Article Text: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has accused Russia of interfering in Britain's 2016 vote to leave the European Union, warning that countries across Europe face the same threat.In excerpts from an episode of “The Rest Is Politics” podcast released on Sunday, Burnham said he asked his advisers after becoming prime minister in July whether Russia had interfered in the Brexit referendum.“I've had the clear answer that yes, there was,” Burnham said.“These things are important now to put clearly on the record and I believe help voters in Germany and France understand that some of this politics is instigated via our enemies, namely Russia,” he added.Burnham's remarks come amid warnings from UK intelligence agencies about the growing threat of Russian interference in Britain's democratic institutions. His comments are believed to mark the first time a British prime minister has publicly acknowledged Russian interference in the Brexit vote.Burnham also said he discussed possible links between Russia and Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz when the two leaders met in Berlin last week.“You know he was saying to me that the AfD are clearly linked to Russia, funded I believe,” Burnham said.“There is certainly misinformation, disinformation that is emanating from Russia into German politics,” he added.In 2020, Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee found that the British government had failed to fully assess the potential impact of Russian state-run media and “troll” accounts on the EU referendum.
Article Summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has accused Russia of interfering in Britain's 2016 vote to leave the European Union. His comments are believed to mark the first time a British prime minister has publicly acknowledged Russian interference in the vote. Burnham also said he discussed possible links between Russia and Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany party.

Article Title: 'Go to jail or be shot’: Trump warns US military secret leakers
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump

US President Donald Trump has a stark warning for those who leak military secrets: face jail or risk being shot. He made the remarks at a rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, on Wednesday (local time), while discussing the US bombing of Iran's nuclear facilities in June 2025.“In my opinion, leakers should be shot,” Trump said, drawing applause from the crowd. “In the old days we used to shoot leakers, you know?”The US President described the B-2 bombers used in the operation as “totally stealth” aircraft that dropped “very large bombs” on the facilities. He further claimed that someone had alerted the news media about the planned attack, adding, “They ought to go to jail or be shot,”This is not the first time Trump has threatened government sources who share information with journalists. When he first took office, he promised to track down the “low-life leakers” who provided the news media with information about his administration's ties to Russia, New York Times reported.Alyssa Farah Griffin, a White House official during Trump's first term, told a Mediaite podcast that she had heard Trump talk about executing a staff member who leaked information.Trump's remarks come as he pushes to restore the use of the federal death penalty, a move he campaigned for after the Biden administration imposed a moratorium on executions.Earlier this month, Trump approved the first legally sanctioned public execution in the US since 1936, paving the way for Nidal Malik Hasan to be killed by firing squad on December 3. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist, killed 13 fellow soldiers at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009.The Trump administration has said the execution would be streamed live. Trump later confirmed that he had “absolutely” agreed to the proposal, while acknowledging that the plan could change.“They are making a determination about that, but he will be killed,” Trump said. “I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes.”The Pentagon had earlier indicated that the execution would be livestreamed, with US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth saying the military would ensure people could watch it. However, Vice President JD Vance expressed uncertainty over whether the broadcast would go ahead.Vance described Hasan's attack as the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside the September 11, 2001, attacks, but said he would not watch the execution if it were streamed live.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has a stark warning for those who leak military secrets. He made the remarks at a rally in Bullhead City, Arizona, on Wednesday. Trump described the B-2 bombers used in the operation as “totally stealth” aircraft.

Article Title: Viola Davis grew up in poverty in Rhode Island; now she and husband Julius Tennon are donating $1.2 million to help local families
Article Text:
PC: Rhode Island Monthly

A $1.2 million donation honours Viola Davis’s mother

From a childhood in poverty to giving back to her Rhode Island roots

What families will be able to access at the new centre

How the new centre will support thousands of Rhode Island residents

For Viola Davis, the place where she grew up remains part of her story, even after a career that has taken her from Rhode Island to Hollywood. The award-winning actress and her husband, Julius Tennon, have announced a $1.2 million investment in Central Falls, the Rhode Island community where Davis once lived. The money will fund a new family engagement centre named after her mother, Mary Alice Davis, whose influence Davis has spoken about in explaining the project. Planned as a permanent base for local services, the centre will bring together food assistance, family support, adult education and employment-related programmes under one roof.The Mary Alice Davis Family Engagement Center is being developed through the couple’s Davis-Tennon Foundation. Its purpose is to give residents a place to find practical support, whether they need help feeding their families, accessing educational opportunities or preparing for work.For Davis, naming the facility after her mother gives the project a personal connection. She has described the decision as a way of honouring a woman who continued to believe in people through difficult circumstances. The centre, she said, would carry that spirit forward by supporting individuals and creating opportunities for families.As reported by WJAR, the $1.2 million investment was announced on Monday, 20 July 2026. Rather than funding a single short-term initiative, the donation is intended to establish a lasting community resource in Central Falls, a city closely connected to Davis’s childhood.Davis grew up in poverty in Rhode Island, an experience that forms an important part of her personal history. She went on to build a career in film, television and theatre, becoming one of the most widely recognised actors of her generation. Her professional achievements have included major industry awards, but her latest investment focuses on a community far removed from the entertainment business.Central Falls was part of the environment in which Davis spent her early years. The new centre offers a way for her and Tennon to direct resources towards residents who may face financial pressures and limited access to services.The couple's contribution is being made through their foundation, which has an existing connection to Rhode Island. The Mary Alice Davis Food Pantry already serves about 3,000 people each month. The new facility is expected to provide a broader base for that work, alongside services aimed at parents, adults seeking new skills and families looking for guidance.Tennon, who is originally from Austin, Texas, has also expressed his commitment to supporting Rhode Island. Although the state is not his birthplace, he and Davis are directing the investment towards a community that holds particular significance for his wife.The planned facility will bring several services together in one location. These include a parent resource centre, a parent university and adult empowerment programmes, giving parents and other residents access to information and opportunities for learning.Food assistance will remain part of the work. The expanded Mary Alice Davis Food Pantry is expected to build on a service that already reaches thousands of people monthly. The centre will also provide workforce development and financial literacy programmes, along with family engagement activities, educational workshops and community events.For people looking for help with more than one issue, having these services in the same place could make it easier to find the right support. Someone visiting for food assistance, for example, may also be able to access parenting resources or information about employment training.The facility will also serve as the permanent administrative headquarters of the Davis-Tennon Foundation. This gives the organisation a local base from which to coordinate its activities and maintain its work in the area.Angelo Garcia, chair of the foundation, said, "Whether someone comes seeking food, parenting resources, educational support, workforce training, or guidance through a difficult season, our goal is simple: one place where people are welcomed, connected, and empowered.”The Mary Alice Davis Food Pantry provides an established starting point for the project. Its reported monthly reach of around 3,000 individuals gives an indication of the demand for food assistance in the community and the role the new centre could play in extending that support.The planned expansion will place the pantry within a wider network of family and adult services. Residents will have access not only to food assistance but also to programmes intended to support education, financial understanding and employment prospects.The centre's effectiveness will depend on how these services are delivered and how well they meet local needs once the facility is operating. The announcement sets out the intended range of programmes, although it does not specify an opening date or provide a detailed timetable for their introduction.By combining food assistance with educational, parenting and employment services, the centre aims to address several practical challenges faced by families in one location.The project also extends the Davis-Tennon Foundation’s existing work in Rhode Island, with the new facility intended to provide a permanent base for its community programmes in Central Falls.
Article Summary: A $1.2 million donation honours Viola Davis’s mother. The actress and her husband, Julius Tennon, have announced a new family engagement centre in Central Falls, Rhode Island. The Mary Alice Davis Family Engagement Center will bring together food assistance, family support, adult education and employment-related programmes under one roof.

Article Title: Florida turned wreckage from the Hurricane Ian-damaged Naples Pier into an underwater habitat: 59 concrete pilings weighing more than 300 tons now sit at Wasmer Reef about 10 miles offshore instead of
Article Text:
From hurricane damage to marine habitat

An established reef gets an expansion

The remaining concrete will also be recycled

Pieces of a historic Florida pier damaged by Hurricane Ian have found a second life beneath the Gulf of Mexico, where they are being repurposed to support marine life. The City of Naples completed the deployment of 59 concrete pilings at Wasmer Reef on April 24, 2026, as part of efforts to rebuild the landmark Naples Pier. According to the city’s announcement, the project was carried out with construction contractor Shoreline Foundation, Inc., and marine and environmental engineers Turrell, Hall & Associates. Local broadcaster Gulf Coast News also reported on the reef deployment. The initiative not only gives the historic pier materials a new purpose but also helps create habitats for marine organisms and supports the Gulf of Mexico’s underwater ecosystem.The transformation follows the extensive damage Hurricane Ian inflicted on Naples Pier on September 28, 2022. The powerful storm destroyed a substantial section of the waterfront structure, leaving parts of the pier collapsed into the Gulf and prompting plans for a complete reconstruction.Originally built in 1888, the pier has long been a popular destination for residents and visitors, known for fishing, wildlife watching and views of the Gulf.The city determined that much of the remaining structure had been compromised and needed replacement to improve safety and resilience.Rather than treating all the demolished concrete as construction waste, officials opted to redirect some of it towards marine habitat restoration. The 59 pilings, weighing more than 300 tons combined, were placed at Wasmer Reef, around 10 miles offshore from Gordon Pass. The deployment was completed under a permit from the US Army Corps of Engineers and overseen by Turrell, Hall & Associates, according to the city.The new material has been added to an existing artificial reef system that was first established in 2015 through a collaboration involving multiple agencies, with funding from BP oil spill grants and private donations. The Naples deployment marks the eighth reef created within the Wasmer site.Artificial reefs can provide hard surfaces and sheltered spaces for marine organisms in areas where suitable natural structures may be limited. Over time, these surfaces can attract organisms that form the base of a wider underwater food web. The city says Wasmer Reef already supports corals, aquatic vegetation, invertebrates, bivalves and tunicates. These organisms help provide food and shelter for fish at different stages of their lives.The old pier pilings will become part of this existing underwater environment, offering additional surfaces for marine organisms to colonise. Dive teams checked conditions at the site before and after the deployment to ensure that the work complied with permit requirements. While artificial reef structures can create habitat, their ecological benefits depend on factors such as water conditions, material suitability and the species able to establish themselves. The newly placed concrete is therefore an addition to an established habitat, rather than an instant replacement for a mature natural reef.The reef deployment is part of a wider effort to reduce waste generated by the pier reconstruction. According to the City of Naples, pilings not selected for the reef have been sent to a recycling facility, where they will be processed into recycled concrete aggregate for use in road construction.This approach gives the removed material two potential uses: some of it will contribute to underwater habitat, while the rest will be converted into a construction resource. The rebuilding project is continuing at the original pier site. The city’s project information describes plans to replace the damaged structure with a stronger, more resilient pier designed to withstand future storms more effectively. The repurposing of the old pilings offers a separate environmental outcome from the reconstruction itself. Material that once supported a popular public landmark will now lie on the Gulf seabed, where it can become part of an evolving marine ecosystem.
Article Summary: The City of Naples completed the deployment of 59 concrete pilings at Wasmer Reef on April 24, 2026, as part of efforts to rebuild the landmark Naples Pier. The initiative not only gives the historic pier materials a new purpose but also helps create habitats for marine organisms and supports the Gulf of Mexico’s underwater ecosystem.

Article Title: What is the ‘Mother of All Bombs’? The massive US weapon in focus over Iran
Article Text:
File photo: The GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB) bomb is pictured in this undated handout photo.

What is the ‘ mother of all bombs ’?

Questions over whether it could hit Iran’s underground sites

A possible escalation

The US military has drawn up fresh strike plans that include using its most powerful non-nuclear bomb against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites, CNN reported on Thursday, citing multiple US officials familiar with military planning.The plans include the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), widely known as the “mother of all bombs”, which could be deployed if US president Donald Trump orders a resumption of combat operations. CNN reported that potential targets include energy infrastructure and the suspected nuclear site at Pickaxe Mountain.The report comes as the Trump administration weighs its options for ending a war that has continued for more than six months, with little indication of an imminent diplomatic breakthrough. Trump has said the US will not allow Iran to acquire a nuclear weapon, but has also faced pressure to bring the conflict to an end.One source familiar with the military planning told CNN that Trump had ordered additional strike packages covering “a lot of energy infrastructure”, with the possibility of using the MOAB. A second source said plans for attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities, including Pickaxe Mountain, explicitly included the bomb.The existence of these plans does not mean a strike has been authorised. A White House official told CNN that the administration does not comment on sensitive military plans that may or may not exist, adding that Trump “keeps all options on the table to ensure that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon”.The Pentagon said it plans for a wide range of operational scenarios to carry out presidential and defence secretary directives.The GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb, or MOAB, is the largest non-nuclear bomb in the US arsenal. It weighs 21,600 pounds, or about 9.8 tonnes, and is designed to produce an enormous blast across a wide area.Unlike a bunker-buster designed to penetrate deep underground, the MOAB detonates before hitting the ground, projecting its blast outward. According to CNN, it can destroy an area equivalent to about nine city blocks, making it suited to large-area targets rather than deeply buried facilities.The weapon was developed during the Iraq War and was conceived in part for psychological effect: its enormous explosion was intended to intimidate enemy forces and pressure them to surrender or avoid fighting. It was designed primarily for use against large concentrations of troops and equipment, as well as hardened structures above ground.Trump first authorised its use in combat during his first presidency, when the US military dropped a MOAB on an Islamic State tunnel complex in Afghanistan in 2017. Afghan officials said the strike killed 36 Islamic State fighters and destroyed tunnels, weapons and ammunition. US and Afghan officials said no civilians were killed in that attack.Despite its destructive power, the MOAB may be of limited use against Iran’s most heavily fortified nuclear facilities.CNN reported that sources familiar with the planning questioned whether the bomb could penetrate deeply enough to destroy the suspected facilities at Pickaxe Mountain, believed to be protected by layers of granite, or other nuclear sites located far underground.One source described the weapon as effective for clearing a large area but said it was “definitely not designed as a deep penetration warhead”.The bomb’s large blast radius could also raise concerns about civilian casualties if it were used against energy infrastructure near populated areas or other non-military sites.Military planners have nevertheless considered the MOAB as a possible means of applying psychological pressure on Tehran. One source told CNN that the weapon could be used to alter the conflict’s current course, even if it was unlikely to force Iran to capitulate or deliver a decisive military victory.The potential use of the MOAB would mark a significant escalation in the US campaign against Iran. CNN reported that military planners have prepared a range of options as the administration searches for a way to end the conflict while securing a political outcome Trump could present as a victory.Some options have reportedly been discussed as a limited show of force before US troops withdraw from the region. But officials have questioned privately whether additional strikes, without a broader strategy, would achieve the administration’s stated goals.CNN also reported that the US military was preparing for possible Iranian retaliation if Trump authorised further attacks, despite the president’s recent pledge to hold off on new strikes before the midterm elections.There has been no reported decision to deploy the MOAB against Iran. Its inclusion in military planning signals that the option is being considered, not that it will necessarily be used.
Article Summary: US military has drawn up fresh strike plans that include using its most powerful non-nuclear bomb against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites. The plans include the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), widely known as the ‘mother of all bombs’ The potential use of the MOAB would mark a significant escalation in the US campaign against Iran.

Article Title: Sara Blakely was selling fax machines door to door when she put $5,000 of her savings into Spanx; 21 years later, Blackstone bought a majority stake in the company at a $1.2 billion valuation
Article Text:
Despite having no formal business education, Blakely developed her first product from her apartment

How Sara Blakely started with $5,000

Blackstone's major investment

Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon join

What changed for Spanx after investment?

In 2000, Sara Blakely was working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson when she decided to start her own business with $5,000 from her savings. Her idea was to develop a new type of women's undergarment that would offer greater comfort and support. However, she had no formal business training, had never attended a business class and had no outside investors. Nonetheless, she went on to establish Spanx, a company that would eventually become a major name in women's clothing.Twenty-one years later, in October 2021, global investment firm Blackstone announced an agreement to acquire a majority stake in the company at a valuation of $1.2 billion. The deal marked a major change for a business that Blakely had built without raising outside investment.According to Blackstone, Blakely would retain a significant ownership stake and continue working with the company's existing management team. She would also become Executive Chairwoman of Spanx.Alongside Blackstone, several prominent women, including Oprah Winfrey, Reese Witherspoon and Whitney Wolfe Herd, joined as investors. Their involvement brought together businesswomen who had previously supported the company or established successful companies of their own.Blakely's journey began while she was still selling fax machines door to door. She wanted to enter the women's shapewear and undergarment market, an industry that was male-dominated at the time.Despite having no formal business education, she worked on developing her first product from her apartment. She also wrote her own patent application for the undergarment she had invented.The company initially focused on shapewear, a category of clothing designed to provide support and create a smoother appearance under other garments. Over time, it expanded beyond original undergarments into several other clothing categories.Its product range eventually included leggings, denim, trousers, activewear, swimwear and intimate apparel. The company also introduced collections such as Perfect Pants, extending its business into everyday clothing.Blakely was also included in TIME magazine's list of the world's 100 most influential people and appeared on the cover of Forbes as the youngest self-made female billionaire.On October 20, 2021, Blackstone announced that funds managed by the investment firm had agreed to acquire a majority stake in Spanx. The agreement valued the entire company at $1.2 billion.Blakely welcomed the agreement while reflecting on how the company had started. “This is a really important moment in time for female entrepreneurs,” she had said.“I started this company with no business experience and very little money, but I cared the most about the customer, and that gave me the courage to launch the company.”The transaction was formally completed on November 18, 2021, when Spanx and Blackstone announced the participation of several additional investors.Among them were television personality and entrepreneur Oprah Winfrey, actress and Hello Sunshine founder Reese Witherspoon, and Bumble founder Whitney Wolfe Herd. Two female-founded investment firms, G9 Ventures and Able Partners, also participated.Winfrey had played a role in bringing the company to public attention during its early years. In 2000, she included the product in her well-known Favorite Thingsselection.Recalling her first experience with the product, Winfrey said, “When Sara first came on The Oprah Show to tell us about her idea for Spanx, I knew it was brilliant.”She added that the company had become a regular part of her wardrobe and expressed support for the company's continued development.Blakely also described the participation of Winfrey and Witherspoon as particularly meaningful because both had supported the brand for years.Under the agreement, Blakely retained a significant equity stake in Spanx and became its Executive Chairwoman. The existing senior management team also remained involved in overseeing daily operations.Blackstone and Spanx announced plans to establish an all-female board of directors. The Blackstone investment team responsible for the transaction was also made up entirely of women.Ann Chung, Global Head of Consumer for Blackstone Growth, said the investment would support product development, international expansion and the company's digital transformation.The transaction also formed part of Blackstone's investments in female-founded businesses, which included Bumble, Hello Sunshine and Hotwire Communications.Beyond her business career, Blakely had also committed to philanthropy. In 2013, she signed the Giving Pledge, promising to donate half her wealth to charitable causes. Through her personal foundation, she had already contributed millions of dollars towards supporting women.
Article Summary: Sara Blakely was working as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson when she decided to start her own business with $5,000 from her savings. Her idea was to develop a new type of women's undergarment that would offer greater comfort and support. In October 2021, global investment firm Blackstone announced an agreement to acquire a majority stake in the company at a valuation of $1.2 billion. Oprah Winfrey and Reese Witherspoon joined as investors.

Article Title: Katy Perry has supported UNICEF since 2013; from visiting vulnerable children in Madagascar to backing global vaccine access and emergency relief
Article Text:
PC: UNICEF

Katy Perry’s UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador role began in 2013

Katy Perry’s UNICEF visit to Vietnam highlighted children’s needs in rural communities

Katy Perry’s UNICEF work earns humanitarian recognition in 2016

Supporting emergency relief and vaccine access

Katy Perry links Daisy’s birth to UNICEF

Katy Perry’s humanitarian work spans children’s rights and LGBTQ+ equality

Katy Perry’s career has largely been defined by chart-topping songs, sold-out performances and a public profile that extends well beyond music. Since 2013, however, the American singer has also held a role with UNICEF, working to draw attention to the circumstances faced by children in vulnerable communities. Her involvement has taken her from a child protection centre in Madagascar to rural communities in Vietnam, while other campaigns have focused on emergency assistance and access to healthcare. Appointed a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador more than a decade ago, Perry has continued to use her visibility to support the organisation’s work. Her contributions have included field visits, public appeals and fundraising efforts linked to the needs of children and families.Perry became a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador in 2013, joining a group of public figures who use their professional reach to support the organisation’s work for children. The appointment reflected her interest in issues affecting young people, particularly those who face barriers to safety, education and basic services.Her early engagement included a visit to Madagascar, where she met children at a centre providing protection for those who had experienced abuse or abandonment.The visit also brought her into contact with young mothers dealing with difficult circumstances. It offered a closer look at the work involved in protecting children beyond the public campaigns and fundraising appeals often associated with international charities.For UNICEF, the role of a goodwill ambassador is partly about reaching audiences who might not otherwise follow its programmes. Perry’s music career gave her an established international platform, which the organisation could use to bring attention to its work in different countries.In 2016, Perry travelled with UNICEF to Ninh Thuan Province in Vietnam. The rural region was among the places where the organisation was working with children and families facing economic hardship and limited opportunities. Her visit helped direct attention towards the circumstances of children living outside the country’s major urban centres.The trip was part of a wider period of engagement with UNICEF, rather than a one-off appearance. Perry had also visited Vietnam in 2015, when she stopped in Ho Chi Minh City to speak at Forbes Vietnam’s first Under 30 Summit. During the event, she moderated a discussion involving young professionals working on initiatives intended to benefit children.These appearances placed her advocacy in two different settings. The field visit brought her into contact with communities served by UNICEF, while the summit provided an opportunity to speak with younger people pursuing projects of their own. Both formed part of her wider involvement in conversations about children’s welfare and opportunities.Perry’s work with UNICEF received formal recognition in 2016, when the United States Fund for UNICEF presented her with the Audrey Hepburn Humanitarian Award at its annual Snowflake Ball. The award acknowledged her commitment to the organisation’s efforts on behalf of children.That year, she also joined fellow UNICEF Goodwill Ambassadors and other public figures in contributing to a global version of John Lennon’s Imagine. The project brought together well-known voices around a familiar song, using their collective reach to support UNICEF’s message.The recognition added a humanitarian dimension to Perry’s public profile, which already included a substantial music career. UNICEF’s biography describes her as one of the bestselling musical artists of all time, with more than 43 million albums sold worldwide and over 30 billion song streams. Her work with the organisation has developed alongside that career, rather than replacing it.Perry’s advocacy has also extended to international emergencies. In 2021, she joined fellow UNICEF Goodwill Ambassadors and other high-profile supporters in urging G7 countries to commit COVID-19 vaccine doses to lower-income nations. The appeal came during a period when access to vaccines remained uneven between wealthier countries and those with fewer resources.The campaign focused on the need to make vaccines available beyond countries that had secured substantial supplies for their own populations. By lending her name to the appeal, Perry helped support UNICEF’s call for a broader international response to the pandemic.Emergency relief has been part of her involvement with the organisation from the beginning. UNICEF identifies her public advocacy for its humanitarian work as one of the ways she has used her position to highlight the needs of children across different regions. Her participation in campaigns has included both longer-term issues, such as child protection, and urgent responses to events affecting families on a large scale.In August 2020, Perry and her partner, actor Orlando Bloom, welcomed their daughter, Daisy Dove Bloom. They announced her birth through UNICEF’s platform and shared the first image of their family in a post that encouraged donations to the organisation.The announcement connected a personal event with UNICEF’s work to support mothers and newborns. The appeal asked people to contribute towards efforts to help ensure that women and babies receive the care they need. Rather than relying solely on a conventional celebrity announcement, the couple used the occasion to direct attention towards maternal and newborn health.The initiative was consistent with Perry’s established relationship with UNICEF. It gave the organisation an opportunity to reach her audience while drawing attention to healthcare needs that affect families around the world, including access to appropriate care during pregnancy and after childbirth.Perry’s public work has also included support for LGBTQ+ equality. She received the Trevor Project’s Hero Award in 2012, before her appointment as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador, and the Human Rights Campaign’s National Equality Award in 2017. In 2018, she received amfAR’s Award of Courage.Her UNICEF role, specifically, centres on children’s rights and wellbeing, with activities ranging from field visits to international appeals.The organisation’s profile of Perry records several milestones in her involvement, including her 2013 appointment, the Vietnam visit, the Audrey Hepburn Humanitarian Award and the vaccine-access campaign. Those activities show how her work with UNICEF has taken different forms over the years, depending on the issue being addressed.More than a decade after her appointment, Perry remains associated with UNICEF’s efforts to improve conditions for children. Her involvement has not been limited to a single campaign or country. It has included direct visits, public advocacy and appeals connected to the health and protection of children and their families.
Article Summary: Katy Perry’s UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador role began in 2013. Her contributions have included field visits, public appeals and fundraising efforts linked to the needs of children and families. In 2016, she was presented with the Audrey Hepburn Humanitarian Award.

Article Title: Once the fastest US ocean liner that carried presidents and celebrities across the Atlantic, SS United States is set to become the world’s largest artificial reef
Article Text:
A record-breaking transatlantic liner

Why the ship stopped sailing

From ocean liner to underwater habitat

The SS United States, a 990-foot ocean liner that carried presidents, dignitaries and celebrities across the Atlantic, is preparing for a final voyage that will take it from a historic passenger ship to an underwater attraction. More than seven decades after its maiden voyage in 1952, the vessel is scheduled to be sunk off Florida’s Gulf Coast in November 2026, where it is expected to become the world’s largest artificial reef. The deployment is planned for the second week of November, subject to final arrangements and weather conditions, according to the SS United States Conservancy.The ship is currently in Mobile, Alabama, where it has undergone environmental remediation and preparations for its planned conversion. Okaloosa County, Florida, which purchased the vessel to prevent it from being scrapped, intends to place it approximately 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin–Fort Walton Beach in the Gulf of Mexico. The project aims to create marine habitat while establishing a new attraction for divers, anglers and tourists.The SS United States made its maiden voyage on July 3, 1952, travelling from New York to Europe. According to the Smithsonian National Museum of American History and the ship’s conservancy, it set a transatlantic speed record on that voyage, capturing the Blue Riband, the informal distinction awarded to the fastest passenger liner crossing the Atlantic.It completed the westbound crossing in three days, 10 hours and 40 minutes, surpassing the previous record held by the British liner RMS Queen Mary.American naval architect William Francis Gibbs designed the ship, which was built at Newport News Shipbuilding in Virginia. Its use of aluminium in parts of its construction helped reduce weight, while its powerful propulsion system gave it exceptional speed for a passenger liner. The vessel was also designed with national defence in mind: during the Cold War, it could potentially have been converted into a troop transport in the event of a military emergency. The US government helped fund its construction, reflecting the strategic thinking behind the project.At 990 feet long and weighing more than 53,000 tons, the ship became a symbol of American engineering and post-war maritime ambition. Its passenger lists included prominent figures from politics and entertainment, and four US presidents travelled aboard during its service: Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower, John F. Kennedy and Bill Clinton. Clinton’s voyage took place when he was a Rhodes Scholar travelling to Oxford, before he became president.Despite its record-breaking performance, the SS United States was overtaken by changes in transatlantic travel. Commercial aviation became faster and increasingly accessible during the 1950s and 1960s, reducing demand for lengthy ocean crossings. The ship was withdrawn from service in 1969 after 17 years of operation.Its future remained uncertain for decades. The vessel was moved to Philadelphia in 1996, where it stayed docked for nearly 30 years. Various proposals sought to restore it as a passenger ship, turn it into a hotel or transform it into a tourist attraction, but none materialised. Financial difficulties and a dispute over docking fees eventually intensified concerns that the ageing liner could be sold for scrap.Okaloosa County ultimately acquired the ship for $1 million in 2024, with the stated intention of creating an artificial reef off Florida. After leaving Philadelphia in February 2025, the vessel was towed to Mobile, where it arrived the following month for preparation. The wider project has been reported to cost approximately $10.1 million, including acquisition, transportation, environmental cleanup and deployment.Before the ship can be submerged, it must be prepared to ensure that hazardous materials do not contaminate the marine environment. Okaloosa County says the required environmental remediation has been completed, but final approvals from the US Army Corps of Engineers and the Environmental Protection Agency remain necessary before deployment can proceed. The November timeline should therefore be treated as a plan rather than a confirmed sinking date.Artificial reefs are submerged structures that provide surfaces and shelter for marine organisms. Over time, organisms such as algae, corals and other invertebrates can colonise suitable surfaces, attracting fish and creating habitat for marine life. The SS United States is expected to become a particularly prominent site because of its size and the potential range of underwater structures it offers. The project is also intended to strengthen the region’s diving and fishing tourism industries.The ship is expected to rest near the USS Oriskany, a former US Navy aircraft carrier that was deliberately sunk off Florida in 2006 and became a major artificial-reef diving site. The SS United States is expected to surpass the Oriskany in size, giving it the distinction of becoming the world’s largest artificial reef if the planned deployment goes ahead as announced.Not every part of the liner will disappear beneath the water. The SS United States Conservancy has retained significant components, including the ship’s iconic funnels and radar mast, for a planned land-based museum and visitor centre near Destin–Fort Walton Beach. The museum is intended to preserve the vessel’s history and engineering legacy for visitors who may later explore its underwater remains.
Article Summary: The SS United States made its maiden voyage on July 3, 1952, travelling from New York to Europe. It set a transatlantic speed record on that voyage, capturing the Blue Riband, the informal distinction awarded to the fastest passenger liner crossing the Atlantic. Its passenger lists included prominent figures from politics and entertainment, and four US presidents travelled aboard during its service: Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower, John F. Kennedy and Bill Clinton.

Article Title: In 2007, Con Edison unveiled a $300 million Bronx substation disguised to read like a rowhouse street; it houses two substations delivering 900MW, and a $47.3 million capacity upgrade is now approved
Article Text:
Representative image

A substation designed to fit the Bronx

How much power it delivers

Why an upgrade is needed now

The $47.3 million Bronx upgrade

Part of a larger grid plan

Why the rowhouse design still matters

When Con Edison unveiled its East 179th Street substation in the Bronx in 2007, it did not look like a typical industrial power facility. The $300 million project was designed to resemble a row of Bronx rowhouses, with a brick facade and a street-level appearance intended to blend into the surrounding neighbourhood. Con Edison said the facility housed two substations capable of delivering 900 megawatts, enough electricity for about 900,000 homes.Nearly two decades later, the substation remains central to the Bronx’s power supply. A New York Public Service Commission order issued in June 2025 approved a $47.3 million urgent upgrade at the facility, including a fifth 138/13 kV transformer and a new 138 kV feeder from the East 179th Street substation. Read more details about it here, as per the report:The East 179th Street project was unveiled in June 2007 as part of Con Edison’s effort to strengthen New York City’s electric delivery system ahead of rising summer demand. The company described it as a $300 million investment that combined two substations into one facility.What made the project unusual was its design. Rather than presenting residents with a large, plain industrial structure, Con Edison built the substation to read like a rowhouse street, using a brick facade that reflected the character of the surrounding Bronx neighbourhood.The design choice reflected a practical reality of urban infrastructure.Substations need to be close to the communities they serve, but they can also be visually intrusive. By making the facility resemble familiar residential architecture, Con Edison sought to reduce its visual impact while still delivering a major increase in electrical capacity.The facility contains two substations with a combined capacity of 900 megawatts. Con Edison said that amount could power approximately 900,000 homes, based on its estimate that one megawatt can supply about 1,000 homes. At the time of the unveiling, Con Edison was investing $1.4 billion across its electric delivery system to meet forecasted peak demand of 13,575 megawatts. The company projected a peak load of 11,780 megawatts for New York City and 1,795 megawatts for Westchester County.The Bronx substation was part of a wider programme that included $739 million for distribution upgrades, $489 million for substation-related projects, and $137 million for transmission improvements. Con Edison said it expected to spend $7.5 billion over the following five years to maintain reliability and support economic growth.The 2025 upgrade is tied to New York’s transition toward building electrification and electric vehicles. The Public Service Commission created an urgent upgrade process to identify projects that must begin before the completion of its broader long-term grid planning process.Con Edison identified 14 potential electric vehicle charging hotspots across its service area, suggested the report. After further analysis, it concluded that four locations required urgent near-term investment, including Zerega Avenue and Hunts Point in the Bronx, as well as East New York and Steinway in Queens.The company found that these areas already had significant electric vehicle charging activity, ranging from early customer interest to projects under construction or in operation. It also projected future demand from electric vehicles and electrified buildings, which would place additional pressure on local grid capacity.The approved Bronx project includes the installation of a fifth 138/13 kV transformer at the Parkchester No. 1 substation. It will be supplied by a new 138 kV feeder running from the East 179th Street substation.The project was approved as part of a broader set of 29 urgent upgrades across New York State. The Public Service Commission authorised development and cost recovery for projects that met its criteria for need, urgency, certainty, and cost-effectiveness.The $47.3 million investment is intended to mitigate risks associated with projected load growth at Zerega Avenue and Hunts Point. By adding transformer capacity and a new feeder, Con Edison aims to support electrification while maintaining reliable service for existing customers.Con Edison’s nine proposed urgent projects had an estimated capital cost of $854.9 million and were expected to add 485 megawatts of incremental system capacity. Those projects included four primary feeder projects, three area substation and sub-transmission projects, and two distribution system programmes.The Bronx upgrade is therefore not an isolated repair. It is part of a wider effort to prepare New York’s grid for increased demand from electric vehicles, heat pumps, and other electrified building systems.The Public Service Commission said the approved projects would help enable building electrification and electric vehicle charging while supporting the state’s efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. It also found that the projects would not disproportionately burden disadvantaged communities.The East 179th Street substation shows that essential infrastructure does not have to look hostile to its neighbourhood. Its rowhouse-inspired design allowed a high-capacity facility to sit within an urban community while reducing the visual impact of heavy electrical equipment.That approach is increasingly relevant as cities invest in grid upgrades to support electrification. New transformers, feeders, and substations will be needed, but residents are more likely to accept such projects when they are designed with local context in mind.The Bronx facility began as a response to rising electricity demand in 2007. Nearly 20 years later, it is being upgraded again, showing how power infrastructure must continually evolve as homes, vehicles, and industries use more electricity.
Article Summary: Con Edison unveiled its East 179th Street substation in the Bronx in 2007. The $300 million project was designed to resemble a row of Bronx rowhouses. A New York Public Service Commission order issued in June 2025 approved a $47.3 million urgent upgrade at the facility, including a fifth 138/13 kV transformer.

Article Title: In 1907, New York’s subway company bought an 1847 Brooklyn townhouse and gutted it; more than a century later the restored-looking façade still hides a ventilation shaft and emergency exit for the tun
Article Text:
Representative image

A home turned into transit infrastructure

Why the facade remained

A five-storey hole beneath the street

Renovated in 1999

Why it stays incognito

A global tradition of hidden infrastructure

Why 58 Joralemon Street still matters

At first glance, 58 Joralemon Street looks like another historic Brooklyn Heights brownstone on a quiet, tree-lined street. Its dark windows and Greek Revival facade blend into the neighbourhood, but the building is not an ordinary home. It conceals a subway ventilation shaft and emergency exit stairway serving the tunnels beneath the East River.
